- accuracy_class: C (that goes in recommendation.accuracy_classes too)
- rated_output: 2 mV/V ± 0.1 mV/V — hmm. Value 2 with nominal... The structured form: value: {nominal: 2, tolerance: 0.1}? The schema says value can be number | {min,max} | string. For 2 mV/V ± 0.1 mV/V I could do value: 2, unit_symbol: "mV/V" and a separate characteristic rated_output_tolerance: 0.1 mV/V. Or keep as string "2 mV/V ± 0.1 mV/V". Strict rules say numbers not strings when possible. I'll do:
  - rated_output: value 2, unit mV/V
  - rated_output_tolerance: value 0.1, unit mV/V

- temperature_range: -10 °C / +40 °C → {min: -10, max: 40}, °C
- apportionment_factor_plc: 0.7 (convert 0,7)
- humidity_class: CH

- output_impedance: 350 Ω ± 3 Ω → output_impedance: 350 Ω, output_impedance_tolerance: 3 Ω
- recommended_excitation: 10 V AC/DC → recommended_excitation: 10 V; excitation type AC/DC — maybe recommended_excitation_type: "AC/DC"
- excitation_maximum: 15 V AC/DC → 15 V
- transducer_material: Stainless steel
- atmospheric_protection: Hermetically sealed/welded
